crime_highlights: the Appellant and his two accomplices pushed their way into the room and assaulted the two occupants
One of the victims was punched in the eye by the Appellant and was injured to the extent that he had to go to the hospital and received five stitches to close the wound
The victims were forced to hand over their two wallets
The Appellant punched and kicked the victim and hit him with a wrench
The Appellant removed the battery from the smoke detector and tried to make the victim eat the battery
rationale_highlights: He was alive to the mitigating significance of the appellant’s early hardship and his fetal alcohol syndrome.
Having been adopted into a non-native family, this offender did not experience many of the systemic background factors often uniquely present in the circumstances of aboriginal offenders
The judge did take into account the mitigating effect of the appellant’s early deprivation which is related to his aboriginal heritage.
note: Appeal court finds Gladue factors only weakly engaged; early deprivation treated as mitigating.

crime_highlights: Mr. Ginnish got up, called her a rat, and threatened to kill her or to get someone to do it
he then attacked her, pushed her down, and punched her
The first blow struck her left eye.
she crawled out of the house and ran to the home of her aunt, Anna Paul
to find her niece, Tina Paul, in a bloodied state, lying on her doorstep
rationale_highlights: The 28 year old appellant did not grow up in a stable environment.
I am obliged to consider all available sanctions other than imprisonment that are reasonable in the circumstances with particular attention to the circumstances of aboriginal offenders
it was taking that section in particular into consideration which dissuaded me, more than anything else from sending you to a federal penitentiary
note: Little detail of the offender's Indigenous background; effect stated only as avoiding federal penitentiary.

crime_highlights: an out-of-control van came up over the curb and struck his vehicle
The impact was so severe that Mr. Blackburn’s vehicle was driven across five lanes of traffic and a median
Mr. Blackburn died of his injuries a few hours later
The out-of-control vehicle was driven by the appellant, Cecil Anthony Boutilier, who had stolen it from a nearby dealership just minutes before
Mr. Boutilier fled the scene on foot
rationale_highlights: Mr. Boutilier’s very difficult life as an African Nova Scotian - Mi’kmaq man was also properly considered
That Mr. Cecil Anthony Boutilier has personally experienced the adverse impact of many factors continuing to plague aboriginal communities since colonization
the trajectory of his life and his criminal behavior leading up to this point is a tragic history of poverty, racial identity confusion, social exclusion and bullying
note: Appeal only on pre-trial credit; para 8 quotes reports, over 350 words; no stated effect.
